challenges.title: GB Domestic Rules and the new tachograph requirement

items.title: Complying with GB Domestic Drivers' Hours
items.text: For purely domestic transport, the Transport Act 1968 Part VI sets a maximum of 10 hours' driving time and 11 hours' duty time per day — barely possible to guarantee by hand across many drivers and routes.

items.title: Light vans requiring tachographs from July 2026
items.text: From 1 July 2026, vehicles between 2.5 and 3.5 tonnes will newly require a tachograph, including a digital tachograph, for cross-border journeys (or cabotage) into the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland.

items.title: Two rulebooks to track at once
items.text: Purely domestic GB transport stays under the GB Domestic Rules, while cross-border light-van journeys will additionally be subject to the tachograph requirement — working out by hand which rule applies to which route is difficult.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off logistics in the UK
solutions.subtitle: From optimised routes to the new tachograph requirement — everything works together.

items.title: Routes automatically optimised
items.text: Klacks sequences stops in the most sensible order — short journeys, time windows met, fewer empty runs.

items.title: 11-hour duty time continuously monitored
items.text: You configure the 11-hour duty-time limit under the Transport Act 1968 as a daily maximum working time; Klacks makes it visible at every route planning stage and warns in good time before it is exceeded. On request, Klacks hard-blocks a breach in automatic planning; with manual planning it stays at a warning. Klacks does not check the 10-hour driving limit — it continues to be evidenced by the tachograph data.

items.title: Domestic and cross-border routes kept separate
items.text: You keep purely domestic GB transport and cross-border light-van routes that will newly require a tachograph from July 2026 in separate groups in Klacks — the tachograph itself covers the tachograph requirement.

items.title: Matching licence categories
items.text: Klacks only assigns routes to drivers with the matching licence category — and warns before documents expire. If a required document is missing or has expired, Klacks refuses the assignment, in manual planning too.

items.title: Installed on your premises: data sovereignty
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure — route and driver data stay with you — and with a locally hosted AI model, they are not passed on to the AI either.

items.title: Klacksy understands your request
items.text: "Plan tomorrow's routes, driver Smith is off sick" is all it takes — Klacksy starts the replanning, and the planning engine takes the configured working-time limits into account.

example.title: Mixed fleet, one plan
example.text: You keep purely domestic GB transport under the GB Domestic Rules and cross-border light-van routes that will newly require a tachograph from July 2026 in separate groups in Klacks — Klacks checks the configured working-time limits for both, and the tachograph evidences driving time.
